models_evaluated: Medtronic Guardian Connect CGM (Guardian Sensor 3) predictive glucose alerts

links.outcome: Time in range with predictive plus threshold alerts vs threshold alone or no alerts
links.effect: Predictive plus threshold alerts showed no TIR difference vs no alerts (3.1% [95% CI −0.8% to 6.9%]; P = .11) or vs threshold only (−0.8% [95% CI −4.7% to 3.0%]; P = .61), despite more alerts (7012 vs 5163).
links.quote: The addition of predictive alerts did not confer further glycemic benefit beyond threshold alerts alone.

models_evaluated: Medtronic Guardian Connect CGM system with Guardian Sensor 3

links.outcome: Time in target glucose range with threshold and predictive alerts enabled versus disabled
links.effect: Threshold alerts versus alerts off: adjusted TIR difference 3.9% [95% CI, 0.1%-7.8%]; Holm-adjusted P = .04. Adding predictive alerts: −0.8% [95% CI −4.7% to 3.0%]; Holm-adjusted P = .61.
links.quote: In this randomized clinical trial of hospitalized adults with diabetes, CGM threshold alerts modestly improved glycemic control compared with CGM use without alerts, whereas the addition of predictive alerts did not confer further glycemic benefit beyond threshold alerts alone.

links.effect: Mean time in range did not significantly differ between the threshold plus predictive alerts group and the threshold alerts only group (-0.8% [95% CI -4.7% to 3.0%]).
links.quote: However, there was no significant difference in the mean TIR between the threshold on and prediction on group and the threshold off and prediction off group (3.1% [95% CI −0.8% to 6.9%]; Holm-adjusted P = .11) or between the threshold on and prediction on group and the threshold on and prediction off group (−0.8% [95% CI −4.7% to 3.0%]; Holm-adjusted P = .61) ( Table 2 ).
